title: A sheaf of modules on a basis extends uniquely to a sheaf of modules
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal B$ a set of open subsets of $X$ which is a basis of the topology, such that $U\cap V\in\mathcal B$ for $U,V\in\mathcal B$, and such that for every $U\in\mathcal B$ every covering of $U$ by members of $\mathcal B$ can be refined to a finite covering of $U$ by members of $\mathcal B$ (each member of the finite covering lies in some member of the given one). Let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of rings on $X$. Suppose given, for every $U\in\mathcal B$, an $\mathcal O(U)$-module $F(U)$, and for $V\subseteq U$ in $\mathcal B$ an additive map $r_{U,V}:F(U)\to F(V)$ with $r_{U,U}=\mathrm{id}$, $r_{V,W}r_{U,V}=r_{U,W}$ and $r_{U,V}(as)=a|_V\,r_{U,V}(s)$ for $a\in\mathcal O(U)$, such that for every $U\in\mathcal B$ and every finite covering $U=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_n$ with $U_i\in\mathcal B$ and $n\ge0$ (for $n=0$, the empty covering of $U=\emptyset$, this says $F(\emptyset)=0$ when $\emptyset\in\mathcal B$) the sequence $0\to F(U)\to\prod_iF(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F(U_i\cap U_j)$ is exact (an element is determined by its restrictions, and a family agreeing on the $U_i\cap U_j$ comes from an element). Then: (a) there is a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $F^{ext}$ on $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] together with $\mathcal O(U)$-linear isomorphisms $\iota_U:F^{ext}(U)\to F(U)$ for $U\in\mathcal B$ with $\iota_V(t|_V)=r_{U,V}(\iota_U(t))$; (b) for every sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal G$ on $X$ and every family of $\mathcal O(U)$-linear maps $\psi_U:F(U)\to\mathcal G(U)$, $U\in\mathcal B$, compatible with the restrictions, there is a unique morphism of $\mathcal O$-modules $\Psi:F^{ext}\to\mathcal G$ with $\Psi_U=\psi_U\circ\iota_U$ for all $U\in\mathcal B$, and $\Psi$ is an isomorphism if all $\psi_U$ are bijective; in particular $(F^{ext},\iota)$ is unique up to unique isomorphism; (c) for $x\in X$ the stalk $F^{ext}_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is the colimit of the $F(U)$ over the members $U\in\mathcal B$ containing $x$ (directed by reverse inclusion), via the maps $F(U)\xrightarrow{\iota_U^{-1}}F^{ext}(U)\to F^{ext}_x$.

source.place: Sheaves on Spaces, Section 009H (label section-bases): Definition 009J (sheaf on a basis), Lemma 009L (label lemma-cofinal-systems-coverings-standard-case: the sheaf condition on a cofinal system of coverings, here the finite ones), Lemma 009M (label lemma-condition-star-sections) and Lemma 009N (label lemma-extend-off-basis) with its proof (sections of the extension are compatible families of germs in the colimit stalks), Definition 009S, Lemma 009T (label lemma-extend-off-basis-module), Lemma 009U (label lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence-modules)

proof.text: Form the additive functor Fab on the basis from F and r, using rid and rcomp. Select coverings whose index type is equivalent to Fin n. The finite-refinement hypothesis, applied to the image of an arbitrary cover, supplies a selected refinement indexed by ULift (Fin n); choose the refinement map from the membership witnesses. Reindex hglue along the finite equivalence. Apply lem-weil-pbc-basis-sheaf-cofinal-coverings to Fab followed by the forgetful functor, obtaining unique gluing on arbitrary basis coverings. Empty index types and n = 0 are included throughout.

source.place: Section 009H, Lemma 009L (label lemma-cofinal-systems-coverings-standard-case) and its proof via Lemma 009K

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-on-basis-extends to Fab with the gluing obtained in step 1. Convert the resulting additive categorical isomorphisms to additive equivalences j. Their restriction compatibility is precisely the input needed by the scalar-action construction of step 3.

source.place: Section 009H, Lemma 009N (label lemma-extend-off-basis) and Lemma 009Q (label lemma-extend-off-basis-structures)

proof.text: Form the presheaf of sets P(W) = O(W) × A(W), where A is the additive sheaf of step 2. On a basis open U define the action by j_U^{-1}(a • j_U(t)); j compatibility and rsmul give naturality on the basis. Use the Mathlib morphism-extension leaf lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis (restrictHomEquivHom and extend_hom_app) to extend this action to a natural map P -> A on underlying sets. Its naturality makes restrictions semilinear. For each of the six Module axioms, restrict its two sides to an arbitrary basis neighbourhood inside W and apply j_U: naturality and the basis action formula reduce equality to the corresponding axiom in F(U). Mathlib section_ext identifies sections whose germs agree, so the axiom holds on W. Construct the presheaf of modules with PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf; its additive presheaf is A, hence it is a sheaf. The j_U become linear equivalences. This constructs clause (a), without arbitrary unproved choices in definitions.

source.place: Section 009H, Definition 009S and Lemma 009T (label lemma-extend-off-basis-module: it suffices to construct the multiplication on the level of presheaves of sets), with the functoriality of Lemma 009O/009U for extending it

proof.text: Given compatible basiswise linear maps, extend their additive maps using restrictHomEquivHom. For linearity on any W, restrict the desired equality to a basis neighbourhood of each point of W. Naturality of the additive extension, semilinearity of restrictions, and its specified basis component reduce to the basiswise linearity; section_ext gives the global equality. Package this as a module-sheaf morphism with PresheafOfModules.homMk. The Mathlib basis hom_ext theorem gives uniqueness. If the basis maps are bijective, compose with the basis linear equivalences to get bijective components of the extended additive sheaf morphism. Apply isIso_iff_isIso_basis and reflection of isomorphisms by SheafOfModules.toSheaf. For another extension G with identifications j, extend the maps j_U^{-1}; they are compatible by injectivity of j_V. Their components are bijective, so asIso gives the desired isomorphism. Morphism uniqueness and Iso.ext prove uniqueness of this isomorphism. This proves clause (b).

source.place: Section 009H, Lemma 009U (label lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence-modules: restriction to B is an equivalence, i.e. fully faithful, with inverse given by Lemma 009T) and Lemma 009O

proof.text: For clause (c), compose phi_U with the additive part of iota_U to obtain compatible additive maps kappa on basis sections of E. Form the sigma type of basis neighbourhoods and their sections and its germ map q to the stalk. By lem-weil-pbc-stalk-germs-on-basis, q is surjective, and two representatives with equal germs restrict equally on a common basis neighbourhood. Compatibility of kappa thus shows that their assigned values are equal. Function.extend produces the induced stalk function with the required germ formula. To prove additivity, represent two stalk elements on basis opens U,V, restrict them to U ∩ V, use additivity of the germ map and of kappa on that intersection. The additive map is unique by surjectivity of q. Translate the germ formula through iota_U^{-1}. Finally, linearity of iota_U^{-1} and PresheafOfModules.germ_ringCat_smul prove the scalar germ identity.

source.place: Section 009H, remarks after Definition 009S and after Lemma 009T (F_x = F^ext_x as O_x-modules, since the members of B containing x form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of x)

Five steps: (1) finite-covering sheaf condition implies gluing for all B-coverings by the cofinal-coverings lemma (new node lem-weil-pbc-basis-sheaf-cofinal-coverings, Stacks 009L/009K; the hypothesis is a finite refinement, which is cofinality); (2) extension as a sheaf of abelian groups (new node lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-on-basis-extends, Stacks 009M/009N/009Q; Mathlib's comparison lemma sheafInducedTopologyEquivOfIsCoverDense with coverDense_inducedFunctor gives it once the gluing condition is shown to be the induced-topology sheaf condition, recorded in its searches); (3) the O-module structure, constructed on presheaves of sets as Stacks 009T says, by extending the action O x F^ext -> F^ext from B and checking the module axioms on B, both with the reviewed Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis (restrictHomEquivHom/hom_ext); (4) clause (b) from the same leaf (restrictHomEquivHom, hom_ext, isIso_iff_isIso_basis) plus linearity on B; (5) clause (c) by the universal property, from the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-stalk-germs-on-basis (exists_mem_germ_eq_of_isBasis, germ_eq_of_isBasis, Stalks.lean:484/491).
